tem-1.name: TEM-1 beta-lactamase
tem-1.resistance_mechanism: Serine beta-lactamase: catalytic Ser70 opens the beta-lactam ring of penicillins and early cephalosporins before they can inhibit penicillin-binding proteins.
tem-1.clinical_note: The archetypal plasmid-borne beta-lactamase; ancestor of the ESBL family, widespread in E. coli and K. pneumoniae.
tem-1.notes: Active site: Ser70 nucleophile, Lys73/Glu166 general base, Lys234/Thr235/Gly236 oxyanion hole. Inhibited by clavulanic acid, tazobactam, avibactam.

kpc-2.name: KPC-2 beta-lactamase
kpc-2.resistance_mechanism: Class A carbapenemase: hydrolyses almost all beta-lactams including carbapenems, the last-line beta-lactams.
kpc-2.clinical_note: KPC is a top-priority WHO/cDC threat; major driver of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) outbreaks.
kpc-2.notes: Inhibited by avibactam, relebactam, vaborbactam; boronic-acid transition-state mimics are active-site inhibitors.

ctx-m-14.name: CTX-M-14 ESBL
ctx-m-14.resistance_mechanism: Extended-spectrum class A enzyme: hydrolyses oxyimino-cephalosporins (cefotaxime, ceftriaxone) that defeat older TEM/SHV enzymes.
ctx-m-14.clinical_note: The globally dominant ESBL family; CTX-M-14 and CTX-M-15 account for most ESBL urinary and bloodstream infections.
ctx-m-14.notes: B3-strand expansion around residues 236-240 gives cefotaxime hydrolysis; avibactam restores susceptibility.

ndm-1.name: NDM-1 metallo-beta-lactamase
ndm-1.resistance_mechanism: Zinc-dependent metallo-enzyme: hydrolyses nearly all beta-lactams including carbapenems. Serine-beta-lactamase inhibitors (clavulanate, avibactam) do NOT inhibit it.
ndm-1.clinical_note: WHO critical-priority carbapenemase; spreads on plasmids across Enterobacterales worldwide. No approved NDM inhibitor as of 2026.
ndm-1.notes: Zn1 ligands His120/His122/His189; Zn2 ligands Asp124/Cys208/His250. Metal-chelating compounds (ciclopirox, captopril, dipicolinate, aspergillomarasmine A) and thiol inhibitors are reported NDM-1 inhibitors - the quantum model scores metal chelation explicitly for this target.

ampc.name: AmpC beta-lactamase
ampc.resistance_mechanism: Chromosomal class C enzyme: hydrolyses penicillins, cephalosporins and beta-lactam/beta-lactamase-inhibitor combinations; not inhibited by clavulanate (it induces AmpC expression).
ampc.clinical_note: AmpC-derepressed P. aeruginosa and Enterobacter cloacae are notoriously multidrug-resistant.
ampc.notes: Motifs SXXK (Ser64-Lys67), YXN (Tyr150-Asn152), KTG (Lys315-Thr316-Gly317); Gln120 partners the R1 amide. Boronates (e.g. the 1KE4 ligand) and avibactam inhibit it.

acr-b.name: AcrB multidrug efflux pump
acr-b.resistance_mechanism: Proton-motive-force-driven pump that expels antibiotics (tetracyclines, quinolones, macrolides, chloramphenicol, rifampicin) straight out of the cell, lowering intracellular concentration below lethal levels.
acr-b.clinical_note: The workhorse multidrug pump of E. coli and Salmonella; efflux is a core mechanism of multidrug resistance and a prime adjuvant target (EPIs like PA beta-N, CCCP, NMP resensitize strains).
acr-b.notes: Distal (deep) binding pocket in the T-state protomer: hydrophobic trap Phe610/Phe615/Phe617/Phe628 + Val605/Ile626 (Vargiu 2015), plus the 5ENO MBX2319 SITE residues Phe178/Ala279/Pro326/Tyr327/Met573/Val612. The switch-loop Phe617 gates substrate export. Pocket defined from inhibitor-bound AcrB structures.
